nodes.name: Hot HCl activation
nodes.procedure: One piece of NF (3 cm × 1.5 cm) was soaked into 10 mL 3 M HCl aqueous solution at 90 °C for 20 min to remove the surface oxides.
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a shows the fabrication process... When NiO on the surface of NF was etched away in 3 M HCl at 90 °C for 20 min

nodes.name: Slow etching nanowire growth
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, the activated NF, denoted as ANF, was placed in a petri dish with the residue acidic solution (~3 M HCl), and sealed with parafilm for 30 h at ambient conditions. At the end of slow etching process, the electrode was thoroughly cleaned with distilled water to remove any extra HCl solution and Ni salt solution, then dried in vacuum oven for test. The final electrode was named as ANF@NW.

aliases: Ni/NiO core–shell nanowires on nickel foam

nodes.characterization_summary: Intense peaks at 560 and 970 cm⁻¹ ascribed to first-order LO and 2LO phonon modes of NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Intense peaks are observed in the case of ANF@NW in the range of 300–1200 cm⁻¹, which can be also related to the stretches of the Ni–O bonds. In detail, the relatively strong peaks at 560 and 970 cm⁻¹ can be ascribed to the first-order longitudinal optical (LO) and 2LO phonon modes of NiO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p₃/₂ at 855 eV and Ni 2p₁/₂ at 873.6 eV (ΔE=18.6 eV) confirm Ni²⁺ oxidation state; Ni⁰ peak at 852.1 eV; O 1s at 531.4 eV (Ni-O) and 532.7 eV (Ni-OH), 35.8% surface hydroxyl groups.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fine spectra of Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ for ANF@NW in Figure 2c (blue curve) appeared at 855 and 873.6 eV, respectively. The energy separation of 18.6 eV agrees well with previous values of Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ in NiO, indicating that the valence state of Ni is +2 oxidation state. Besides the characteristic binding energy of Ni²⁺, the peak ascribing to Ni⁰ was observed at binding energy of 852.1 eV... O 1s core level spectra of ANF@NW can be deconvoluted into two peaks centered at 531.4 and 532.7 eV... about 35.8% hydroxyl groups on the very surface of NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiO core-shell nanowire confirmed; Ni(111) lattice fringe at 0.201 nm; NiO (220) plane amorphous.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiO/Ni core–shell nanowire is illustrated in Figure 3b,c, where a lattice fringe is spaced by 0.201 nm, corresponding to the (111) plane of metallic Ni. On the other hand, the lattice fringes corresponding to (220) plane of NiO was not observed... indicating the amorphous phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of O elements confirms intact NiO thin layer coverage on Ni metal core.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni and O elemental mapping images in Figure 4 confirmed the uniform distribution of O elements, indicating the intact coverage of NiO thin layer on the surface of Ni metal.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area 24.2 m²/g; pore volume 0.034 cm³/g; mesopores <3.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area of ANF@NW is 24.2 m² g⁻¹ whereas ANF and NF illustrate BET surface area of 1.24 and 0.64, respectively. Meanwhile, the porous volume of ANF@NW was found to be 0.034 cm³ g⁻¹... confirmed the existence of mesopores with average pore diameter less than ≈3.5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Presence of Ni metal confirmed before and after electrochemical testing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of Ni metal before and after test was confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) in Figure S16 (Supporting Information).
